question: Can a grammar extension that raises ClayCode corpus parse coverage preserve semantics-bearing operator identity, or can Lark tree shaping silently erase operators while parsing still succeeds?

hypothesis.claim: For semantics-bearing unary operators under the current Lark configuration, named terminals plus explicit tree aliases preserve operator identity across the parser-to-AST boundary, while anonymous literal operators inside conditionally inlined ? rules can be erased when keep_all_tokens is false.

strongest_counterhypotheses.claim: The observed negation defect is a one-off grammar typo limited to ! and does not justify a general semantic-token invariant.
Even if unary-token survival is repaired, the new evaluator is not generally semantically valid because independent comparison-chain semantics remain unresolved.

external_evidence.finding: Lark filters unnamed literals by default and conditionally inlines ? rules when one child remains after filtering; named terminals and aliases preserve tree information needed by a Transformer/lowerer.
The official tutorial demonstrates filtered literals and alias-driven tree preservation.
Equivalence and round-trip properties are appropriate high-leverage tests for parsers, serializers and compiler-like boundaries.

observations.result: all three collapsed to the same post-filter parse-tree shape
observations.named_terminal_alias_variant: preserved one and two nested not_expr nodes

out_of_box_experiment.name: OPERATOR_SURVIVAL_METAMORPHIC_MATRIX
out_of_box_experiment.limits: This generalizes the tree-shaping failure class in bounded minimal grammars; it does not prove every full ClayCode operator production is currently safe.

concurrent_counterevidence.finding: Evaluator comparison-chain semantics are unresolved; current Boolean left-fold can disagree with adjacent-pair interpretation, and the concurrent bounded metamorphic lane reported 1596 divergences in 12348 cases (12.925%) under that reference interpretation.
concurrent_counterevidence.consequence: Do not promote F-V01-02 evaluator completeness from the negation repair or corpus-coverage increase. Resolve/fix owner-authoritative comparison-chain semantics separately.

supported: PR #314's silent negation-erasure finding is mechanism-supported by official Lark tree-construction behavior and a local Lark 1.3.1 reproducer.
Semantic operator survival should be a first-class parser-to-AST invariant, not merely a corpus parse-success metric.
The permanent branch gate converts that invariant into executable regression coverage on the same pinned target workflow.
not_supported: 90% parse coverage does not imply 90% executable semantic correctness.
The complete ClayCode evaluator is not PASS; PR #316 supplies active counterevidence.
No target-VPS PASS is claimed for the new operator-survival gate in this receipt.

architecture_delta.name: SEMANTIC_TOKEN_SURVIVAL_INVARIANT
architecture_delta.proposed_rule: Any syntax token whose presence changes semantics must survive into an explicit typed AST distinction. Do not rely on anonymous literals inside conditionally inlined ? rules unless an executable differential/property gate proves the intended semantic distinction survives tree shaping.
architecture_delta.rollback: Remove the new regression gate/workflow step and restore prior grammar only if a stronger parser construction provides equivalent or better semantic-survival evidence.
